item.title: Brazil: defeated Flávio Bolsonaro ordered to surrender passports
item.description:
This article was published in partnership with Agência Pública , Brazil’s largest nonprofit newsroom . Two weeks before the second and decisive round of the Brazilian presidential elections in October, US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was in Rio de Janeiro for the multiday celebration of his son Conor’s wedding . The Kennedy scion married singer Giulia Be, a pop star born into a Brazilian right-wing clan, the Marinho family, who are close allies of the disgraced former President Jair Bolsonaro. The nuptials took place at the Our Lady of Mount Carmel Church in historic downtown Rio, which once served the Portuguese royalty that colonized Brazil for more than 300 years. A week later, supporters of then-presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro carried an inflatable missile with the words “Trump nuke Brazil” in English at a rally in the city of São Paulo. item.title: Climate Activists Celebrate Lula’s Win in Brazil, but Warn the Fight Is Far From Over
item.description:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of Brazil celebrates after the results of the general election day on Oct. 25, 2026 in Sao Paulo, Brazil. Photo by Alexandre Schneider/Getty Images. When Brazil’s first round results came out, the Brazilian left went into a panic. Pollsters undercounted far-right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro’s tally, who ended up first with 47% of the vote. Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula Da Silva, a veritable legend of the Latin American left, fell to second place, with 45%, a difference of over 2 million votes. Sentiment around Brazil’s left electorate was negative and defeatist. It seemed quite impossible to turn around such a solid Bolsonaro advantage. But just when morale was at its lowest, Lula reshuffled his campaign team, incorporating the 41-year-old Governor of Piauí State, Rafael Fonteles. item.title: Jordan says its military struck 'militant hideouts' in Syria after deadly church attack
item.description:
Jordanian air force says it carried out strikes against ‘terrorist groups’ tied to killing of nine in Karak Jordan has carried out airstrikes against armed groups in Syria in retaliation for Friday’s attack on a Greek Orthodox church in the southern Jordanian city of Karak that killed nine people, the Jordanian air force has said in a statement. It said the operation “resulted in the killing and wounding of many members of these terrorist groups and the destruction of a number of their vehicles”. It did not specify who the groups were or the precise location of the strikes. Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or drought, Putellas wins third crown
item.description:
Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d’Or on Monday after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season. Spain’s Alexia Putellas claimed her third women’s award after helping Barcelona win the Champions League, ending teammate Aitana Bonmati’s three-year reign.

item.title: Tens of thousands of Israelis living abroad are expected to fly in for pivotal vote
item.description:
Israelis can’t vote from abroad, so tens of thousands of expats are expected to fly home for the election. At Tel Aviv airport, supporters of opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot are already waiting at arrivals. A “Fly and Vote” initiative helps expats organise their trip, despite a failed petition from Netanyahu’s Likud party to restrict it. With polls predicting a tight race, every vote could count, and the result will decide the Prime Minister’s fate.

item.title: iPhone Duo owners report cracks in Apple’s first foldable handset
item.description:
Apple’s $2,000 folding phone, the iPhone Duo, came out just two days ago and people are already seeing big fat creases down the middle of the folding screen, and some devices are cracked in the same specific spot too. People waited in line overnight at Apple stores to get this thing, and now we’re seeing photos of heinous cracked and creased-up Duos all over social media. In some cases, the phone screens have cracked along the crease, causing a crashout people are now calling “crackgate.” “Had my iPhone Duo for about six hours and had probably opened it fewer than 20 times,” one person wrote on Reddit’s r/iPhoneDuo . “I was showing it to a friend, and as I opened it, I felt something around the internal hinge, underneath the screen. As I continued opening it, I heard an audible crack, and the screen broke right along the hinge.” “How long before I join crack gang?” someone else wrote ,…

item.title: Potential WNBA finals decider to be played at 12.30pm on a Thursday
item.description:
The WNBA was faced with the following issue: After the first four games of the WNBA Finals, played at the raucous 18,064-seat Chase Center in San Francisco and then at equally raucous 17,044-seat State Farm Arena in Atlanta, the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream are tied at two games apiece. The teams will play a Game 5 in San Francisco on Monday night, and a now-necessary Game 6 on Thursday in Atlanta, where the Dream’s primary venue, Gateway Center Arena, seats just 3,500. You'll recall that this was the exact issue the league and the Dream had to scramble to resolve before the Finals started. Games 3 and 4 were originally scheduled for nights when State Farm Arena was already booked for a Sombr concert and the Atlanta Hawks' home opener.
